answer: We define a mechanism where dynamic opportunity-cost bonds enforce capital lockup against an infinite ocean of sybil identities, requiring zero-knowledge verifiable delay primitives to gate ingress. By mapping validator participation to a subgame-perfect punishment matrix, we ensure that the cost of maintaining a jade stake across fragmented accounts creates an island of negative expected utility for any attacker. Multi-agent stability converges when unilateral deviation into identity multiplication strictly reduces marginal yield.
